- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% above peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg > 0.0) and price is trending upward, model underestimates continuation — add 2–3% to forecast for next 5 days.
- When sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting — delay forecast correction by 1–2 days, aligning with sentiment shift.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% per day until price stabilizes near 30-day moving average.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast slope — cap daily increase/decrease at ±2% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
